tob-10096: Richard Rolle, a fourteenth-century English hermit, writes plain guides to the contemplative life for ordinary readers. His works — written partly in Middle English — teach how to turn from worldly cares toward prayer, meditation, and love of God. They give a rare, firsthand voice of medieval English spirituality, direct and personal rather than scholarly.
tob-10496: Julian of Norwich, an English anchoress who lived walled into a small cell by a church, recorded sixteen visions of Christ’s love in what became the first book in English known to be written by a woman. Her most famous line — ‘all shall be well, and all shall be well’ — has comforted readers for six centuries. This is medieval mysticism at its most tender.
tob-0096: Johann Weyer — leech to the Duke of Cleves — penned the first doctor’s broadside at the witch-hunts, holding accused witches for gloomy old women, not devil-worshippers. His great work, excerpted here as De Lamiis, enraged the demon-hunters. The book marks the birth of mind-doctoring on witchcraft.
tob-4096: H. Kern’s Englishing of the Lotus Sutra — the Saddharma Pundarika — gives one of Buddhism’s best-loved scriptures. Its parables of the burning house and the lost son preach rescue for all. Kern’s scholar’s version graced the Sacred Books of the East.
tob-10796: Arthur Lloyd’s Hinduism and Buddhism — An Historical Sketch — traces the two faiths from the Vedas through their spread across Asia. The missionary-scholar wrote with sympathy and learning. The book remains a clear historical introduction to the Eastern religions.
cia-0000113196: An untitled 1945 document of names and descriptions of persons — the truncated title hides the case they belonged to. Pages of names were the raw material of wartime intelligence: watch lists, suspect rolls, contact sheets. The entry is a roster without its story, waiting for a historian to supply one.
cia-0000119696: A January 1954 study of Soviet-bloc economic warfare capabilities and possible courses of action. The Cold War had an economic front: embargoes, trade manipulation, and resource pressure. The document maps the weapons of that quiet war — fought with contracts instead of guns.
cia-0000124296: A December 1957 study of the Soviet rocket program and its earth satellites. Two months after Sputnik, the CIA was building the definitive technical file on Moscow's space effort. The document shows analysis catching up with events — the slow work of understanding a shock.
cia-0000132296: Situation Report 605 on military developments, its paragraph header deleted. The censors trimmed the specifics, but the number keeps its place. The entry is a redacted battle update — the war's progress, partially veiled.
cia-0000132496: A January 1961 estimate of probable international reactions to possible American courses of action against Cuba — the truncated title withholds the options. Before the Bay of Pigs, Washington gamed out the world's response. The document is the invasion, war-gamed: the fallout, forecasted.
cia-0000132596: An August 1960 report on possible Cuban involvement in subversive activity in Venezuela. Havana's hand was suspected behind Caracas's unrest. The document is the suspicion, investigated: the neighbor's troubles, traced to the island.
cia-0000135796: An estimated 1995 study: the CIA and Guatemala assassination proposals, 1952 to 1954. The darkest file — murder, proposed as policy. Declassified decades later, the document is the moral reckoning: the proposals, exposed.
cia-0000135896: A 1954 report by a deleted Mr. on the OAS conference. The hemisphere's parliament, observed — the observer, hidden. The entry is the report: the conference, covered — the author, censored.
cia-0000136096: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN on the King program. Another cryptonym, another project. The entry is the reference: the program, named — the details, coded.
cia-0000136196: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN for ONTRICH on SECANT, vehicles, a Quetzaltenango contact, and pilots — the truncated title compresses the agenda. The logistics list. The entry is the bundle: the items, covered.
cia-0000136296: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN on the need to visit STORAX. The cryptonym site, to be seen. The document is the visit: the need, stated — the place, coded.
cia-0000136396: A 1954 cable to LINCOLN on an HGG-A-563 report of a conversation between deleted persons — the truncated title cuts off the rest. The overheard talk, reported. The entry is the conversation: the parties, hidden.
cia-0000136996: The PBSUCCESS situation report number 3, 1954. The early count. The document is the number: the third, reported.
un-sc-res-1396: Security Council Resolution 1396, adopted in 2002 — aligned. The Council's business continued. The designation and year endure; the act is in the text.
un-sc-res-1496: Security Council Resolution 1496, cataloged with the year 1973 — the numbering belongs to 2003, a deep mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted.
un-sc-res-1696: Security Council Resolution 1696, adopted in July 2006 — the Iran nuclear resolution, demanding Tehran suspend uranium enrichment and making the IAEA's requirements mandatory. The Council's first binding act in the nuclear standoff. The resolution is the demand: the enrichment, suspended — or else.
un-sc-res-1996: Security Council Resolution 1996, cataloged with the year 2009 — the historical record places this South Sudan mission resolution in July 2011, creating UNMISS for the newborn nation. The designation is kept; the catalog's date is questioned.
cia-0000135696: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000135696. The invasion year's papers, another set. The document is the set: the brigade, documented.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d96: President Roosevelt to Prime Minister Churchill, November 5, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 96. Washington to London. The message is the link: the allies, in touch.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d196: The President to the ambassador in the Soviet Union, Harriman, November 8 — the truncated title cuts off the year — Document 196. The White House wrote Moscow's envoy. The message is the envoy: Harriman, instructed.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d296: The Secretary of State to the President, November 23, 1943 — Document 296. A third. The memo is the tripling: the paper, flowing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d396: A draft declaration on Iran — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 396. The Allies' promise to the occupied host nation, in draft. The draft is the promise: Iran, assured.
a-brief-history-of-the-united-states-pg6: John Bach McMaster, one of the great tellers of the nation's past, sums up the story of the United States for students in this clear, trusted textbook. From early days through the modern age he keeps the tale moving while covering the ground. A classroom classic that taught young readers how their country came to be.
arxiv-2605-08896: A model can be right and still fragile — one nudge to the input flips its answer. Zhuoyun Li, Boxuan Wang, Jinwei Hu, Xiaowei Huang, and Yi Dong propose FragileFlow, using spectral control to tame those correct-but-fragile predictions in foundation models. The 2026 paper targets robustness where accuracy alone misleads.
arxiv-2605-08996: Symbolic accelerators crunch graph-structured computations, but bloated graphs waste silicon. Tiffany Yu, Rye Stahle-Smith, Darssan Eswaramoorthi, and colleagues simplify those graphs with machine learning before they hit the hardware. The 2026 paper is about making symbolic computation leaner and faster.
arxiv-2605-09096: Neural operators learn mappings between whole functions — fields, not just vectors — and U-Nets organize computation hierarchically. Enrique Hernández Noguera and colleagues bridge the two with SpectraNet, aiming for stable autoregressive prediction. The 2026 paper merges spectral operator learning with deep hierarchies.
arxiv-2605-09196: Rigid bodies — tumbling boxes, clanking robots — obey strict dynamics that transformers were not built for. Zhiyang Dou, Minghao Guo, Haixu Wu, and Doug Roble teach transformers rigid dynamics with RigidFormer. The 2026 paper is physics-flavored deep learning for solid objects in motion.
arxiv-2605-09296: AI-generated images look perfect at a glance but betray themselves in microscopic statistical defects invisible to the eye. Boxuan Zhang, Jianing Zhu, Qifan Wang, and colleagues detect fakes via local distributional shifts — small regions where the statistics go wrong. The 2026 paper catches synthetic images by their tiny tells.
arxiv-2605-09496: Reasoning in LLMs may live in subspaces that do not care about format — math, code, prose all share the machinery. Aojie Yuan and Zhiyuan Su look beyond language for format-agnostic reasoning subspaces. The 2026 paper hunts the universal circuitry of thought.
arxiv-2605-09596: Muonic atoms — with a heavy muon orbiting instead of an electron — probe the nucleus exquisitely, and the nucleus is not a point. Doğa Yaşar and Bastian Sikora compute finite nuclear size corrections to hyperfine structure. The 2026 paper is precision atomic physics.
arxiv-2605-09696: Discovering a system's governing equations from data needs the right basis functions — and choosing them by hand is deeply limiting. Mohammad Amin Basiri and Charles Nicholson generate the basis functions automatically. The 2026 paper discovers nonlinear dynamics without hand-picked dictionaries.
arxiv-2605-09796: Misophonia — when everyday sounds trigger rage or panic — is poorly understood, and sufferers' voices go unheard. Tawfiq Ammari reports lived experience of misophonia and sensory trauma, arguing for trauma-informed design. The 2026 paper centers the real people behind the condition.
arxiv-2605-09996: Omnimodal personalization — across text, image, and audio — needs systematic benchmarking and improvement; Omni-Persona does both. Yeongtak Oh, Dongwook Lee, Sangkwon Park, and colleagues build the benchmark. The 2026 paper is personalization across every modality. It personalizes skillfully in every sense.
arxiv-2605-10096: Steinhaus longimeters — measuring devices with a classical pedigree — randomly shifted, and Buffon discrepancy: geometric probability with a needle-drop flavor. Samuel Korsky investigates both. The 2026 paper is discrepancy theory. It measures precisely how evenly randomly dropped needles fall.
plos-pone-0003396: Brain scanners revealed pain rewriting the brain in this 2008 study. Patients with trigeminal neuropathic pain, a chronic facial-nerve condition, showed both structural shrinkage and matching functional changes in the cortex. The damage lined up with the disease, evidence that long-running pain is not just a signal the brain receives but a condition that physically reshapes it.
plos-pone-0003496: Tuberculosis researchers spotlighted a master switch in this 2008 paper. The regulator protein PhoP controls virulence in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, and deleting it weakens the bacterium enough to make it a live-vaccine candidate. The review-style study pieces together PhoP's role in the intricate puzzle of TB's staying power, with preclinical vaccine promise.
plos-pone-0003596: Kidney researchers found an alarm receptor driving reperfusion damage in this 2008 paper. Toll-like receptor 4 detects the danger molecules spilled by injured tissue, and the team showed it coordinates the innate immune assault after renal ischemia. Blocking that coordination could spare kidneys the friendly fire that follows restored blood flow.
plos-pone-0003696: In 2008, Pinto, Melo-Cristino, and Ramirez built a better yardstick for microbe sorting. Their confidence interval for the Wallace coefficient lets researchers judge how well two clustering schemes of bacteria agree. The tool brings honest error bars to the everyday work of microbial typing.
plos-pone-0003796: Premi, Srivastava, and Panneer found a patchwork Y chromosome in this 2008 paper. Girls with Turner syndrome carrying Y-chromosome bits showed striking mosaicism, with SRY and DAZ genes duplicated in tandem. The findings matter because Y fragments raise the risk of gonadoblastoma tumors.
plos-pone-0003896: A 2008 stem-cell study got lab-grown heart cells multiplying. Yamanaka, Zahanich, and Wersto boosted proliferation in monolayer cultures of ES-derived cardiomyocytes. The enhanced growth brings replacement heart tissue a step closer to reality.
plos-pone-0003996: In 2008, Sabath, Landan, and Graur solved a puzzle of genes written over each other. Their method estimated selection strength separately for each overlapping gene in the pair. Overlapping codes had long hidden adaptation's fingerprints until this neat statistical disentangling. The tool lets evolution's signature be read even in the most crowded genomes.
plos-pone-0004096: In 2009, Moorthy, Gupta, and Bhosale probed a life-saving trade-off in India. Single and extended nevirapine doses cut breast-milk HIV transmission in Indian infants. But the drug seeded nevirapine resistance in some babies. The hard balance shapes infant prophylaxis policy today.
plos-pone-0004196: In 2009, Mostowy, Tham, and Danckaert found cell scaffolds fighting germs. Septins regulated bacterial entry into host cells. The filament proteins helped cells resist invasion. The finding names septins as innate defenders. The work adds a new player to the cell's defense roster.
plos-pone-0004296: In 2009, a team found oxidation flipping prions badly. Oxidized methionine on prion helix-3 loosened its tight fold. The rusty switch enabled deadly prion change fast. The neat chemistry marks a change trigger. The finding suggests antioxidant shields against prion disease.
plos-pone-0358596: University teachers are adopting generative AI — or quietly resisting it. This paper extended the technology acceptance model to link teachers’ perceived GenAI competency with their intention to keep using it. The results tell universities what actually drives lasting AI adoption in teaching, beyond the initial hype.
plos-pone-0354696: Yellow fever mosquitoes shrug off many repellents — but hemp might faze them. This study tested hemp leaf extracts and cannabidiol for toxic and repellent effects against adult female Aedes aegypti. The plant-based results offer a greener weapon against one of the world’s deadliest disease vectors.
plos-pone-0357796: Mastitis costs dairy farmers dearly — and Sahiwal cattle deserve better defenses. This paper identified differentially expressed lncRNAs and candidate ceRNA networks across mastitis stages in this hardy breed. The RNA networks reveal how the udder’s molecular defenses shift as infection progresses from mild to severe.
plos-pone-0357296: Mesenchymal stromal cells can donate their mitochondria to failing neighbor cells — cellular organ transplants. This paper characterized MSC-mediated mitochondrial transfer to healthy and diseased intervertebral disc cells. The transfer mechanism offers a genuinely new angle on treating degenerative disc disease.
plos-pone-0354796: Men and women read social cues differently — and the gap widens where social function is impaired. This study examined sex differences in social cognition using a sample enriched for social dysfunction. The insights refine our understanding of the social brain and why it misfires differently by sex.
plos-pone-0354096: Asiatic lions — fewer than a thousand remain — desperately need room beyond their single stronghold. This paper made the case for Barda wildlife sanctuary as a potential second stronghold for the species beyond Gir. A second home could be the difference between survival and catastrophe for these cats.
plos-pone-0335296: Leopards share Sri Lankan farmland with people — by keeping carefully different hours. This study showed these leopards employ temporal partitioning as a coexistence mechanism in human-dominated, unprotected agricultural landscapes. The time-sharing arrangement keeps an uneasy peace between predator and farmer.
plos-pone-0357496: Careers should sustain people, not consume them. This paper presented the Polish adaptation and validation of the sustainable career scale — a tool for measuring whether work supports a good life over time. The validated instrument lets Polish researchers and employers assess career sustainability rigorously.
plos-pone-0356796: Carbon monoxide poisoning disrupts the body’s breathing chemistry in surprisingly complex ways. This paper examined hypocapnia — abnormally low blood CO2 — in acute CO poisoning as a complex interaction reaching beyond simple metabolic compensation. The refined physiology should improve emergency care for poisoning victims.
plos-pone-0356496: Who receives invasive coronary angiography isn’t determined by medical need alone. This national claims database study examined the economic drivers and systemic disparities in invasive coronary angiography. The data expose uncomfortable inequities in cardiac care — who gets the catheter and who doesn’t.
plos-pone-0355996: Detecting milk fat content demands highly sensitive sensors. This paper used hybrid machine learning to optimize a multilayer surface plasmon resonance sensor for high-sensitivity milk fat detection. The optimized sensor guards dairy quality with precision the industry can trust.
plos-pone-0355196: Mosquitoes are evolving cross-resistance that defeats multiple insecticides at once. This paper showed metabolic resistance drives cross-resistance in Aedes albopictus to both pyriproxyfen and pyrethroid insecticides. The finding seriously complicates vector control — killing mosquitoes gets harder every year.
plos-pone-0357096: The desert rose plant may hide weapons against lung cancer. This computational study identified and evaluated Adenium obesum phytochemicals as potential EGFR inhibitors for targeted therapy against non-small cell lung cancer. The in silico screen nominates natural compounds as drug leads worth testing in the lab.
plos-pone-0356996: The pupil betrays where attention goes — if you know how to read it. This paper developed an estimation method for identifying the attended object using spatial frequency selectivity in pupillary response. The method reads focus straight from the eyes, opening new possibilities for attention research.
plos-pone-0356596: Anti-VEGF eye injections save sight in wet macular degeneration — but bleeding inside the eye is a feared complication. This study compared the risk of intraocular hemorrhage among exudative AMD patients treated with different anti-VEGF agents. The head-to-head comparison helps ophthalmologists choose the safest drug.
plos-pone-0356696: Growing up alongside an autistic sibling shapes a childhood in profound, rarely studied ways. This paper gathered the perspectives of neurotypical siblings — the echoes of autism in family life as they live it. Their candid accounts reveal pride, resentment, protectiveness, and wisdom that researchers and support services have largely overlooked.
plos-pone-0355396: Early recovery from alcohol use disorder is when relapse risk runs highest — and predicting lapses could save lives. This longitudinal observational study evaluated cellular communication sensing — data from smartphones — for lapse risk prediction during that fragile window. The findings suggest our phones’ behavioral traces can flag impending relapse, opening the door to just-in-time interventions that reach people before they drink.
plos-pone-0351296: Qurayyah Painted Ware — striking ancient pottery from Arabia — tells a story of branding millennia before marketing. This paper traced its genesis, transformation, and diffusion. The archaeological narrative reveals how a distinctive ceramic style became a cultural signature across ancient trade networks.
plos-pone-0356296: People with HIV who smoke face compounded heart risks — and nicotine metabolism speed may modulate them. This paper examined how the rate of nicotine metabolism affects myocardial infarction risk among smokers with HIV. The findings could personalize smoking cessation and cardiac prevention in this vulnerable group.
plos-pone-0354896: Osteosarcoma — bone cancer — demands fast, accurate MRI diagnosis. This systematic review surveyed recent advances in deep learning applications for AI-based osteosarcoma diagnosis on MRI. The review maps which neural network approaches actually work — separating genuine diagnostic progress from AI hype in musculoskeletal oncology.
plos-pone-0355296: Can digital health tools ease loneliness in older adults — or do they deepen isolation? This paper published a scoping review protocol on digital health’s impact on loneliness and social isolation in the elderly. The planned review will separate the technologies that genuinely connect from those that merely distract.
plos-pone-0355596: Immersive VR training generates rich physiological data — if sensors and AI can interpret it. This scoping review mapped physiological sensing systems and AI-based signal analysis in immersive VR learning and training. The synthesis charts a field poised to make virtual training genuinely adaptive to learners’ bodies.
plos-pone-0350296: Heart disease driven by salty diets and kidney dysfunction will burden G20 nations for decades. This paper tracked trends and projections of that ischemic heart disease burden from 1990 to 2050. The sixty-year projections are a policy alarm bell — showing where prevention could avert millions of cardiac deaths.
plos-pone-0355496: DNA barcoding generates oceans of data on the BOLD platform — and researchers need better tools. BOLDconnectR is an R package for streamlined retrieval, transformation, and analysis of BOLD barcode data. The open-source package democratizes large-scale biodiversity informatics.
plos-pone-0346396: Chinese social media burns with workplace burnout discourse — and computation can map it. This paper analyzed the discourse, sentiment, and resonance of burnout on Chinese social media. The findings reveal how an entire generation articulates exhaustion — and what that collective voice demands.
europmc-pmc2861696: White blood cells cast DNA nets to snare fungi, and this 2010 paper studies the trick against Aspergillus. The authors show trap-making in lung tissue depends on invading neutrophils and varies with conditions. Their work details a front-line defense. The findings matter for patients whose nets fail.
europmc-pmc2909996: Identifying fungi from soil DNA needs a reliable barcode. This 2010 paper tests ITS as an environmental DNA barcode for fungi with computer simulations, revealing potential PCR biases. The authors' in silico probe warns of skewed results. Their caution improved fungal surveys.
europmc-pmc2913796: Obesity smolders with low-grade inflammation that never quite goes out. This 2010 review covers lasting inflammation in obesity and the metabolic syndrome, the cluster of blood sugar, pressure, and lipid troubles. The authors connect fat-driven fire to diabetes and heart disease. Their overview traces a root cause of today's chronic diseases.
europmc-pmc3034196: RTX proteins form a huge toxin clan. This 2010 review covers the sprawling RTX family, all shipped out by one secretion system. The authors survey the clan's tricks. Their overview aids germ science. Whooping cough toxin is a famous member. Vaccine designers target these shared machines.
europmc-pmc3098796: Stem cell trials got a field guide. This 2011 paper surveys clinical trials testing stem cell therapies. The authors map the crowded landscape. Their overview guides the field. Eye and heart trials led the pack. The guide warns of unproven clinics.
europmc-pmc6510296: Mitochondria are the cell's power plants, and when they falter, the body may stop responding properly to insulin - a hallmark of type 2 diabetes. Scientists still debate which problem causes the other. This review traces the molecular links between failing mitochondria and insulin resistance, and looks at how diet and habits that revive the power plants might help prevent or treat diabetes.
europmc-pmc6517696: Bacteriophages are viruses that kill bacteria while leaving human cells alone - a tempting weapon against drug-resistant infections. This narrative review weighs the promise against the pitfalls: phages can be exquisitely specific and evolve with their prey, but dosing, immune clearance, and regulation complicate real-world use. The authors see them as partners to antibiotics, not replacements.
europmc-pmc6519796: Standard heart-disease risk scores use a handful of factors and miss many future patients. Researchers unleashed automated machine learning on health records from 423,604 UK Biobank volunteers, letting algorithms find their own patterns. The resulting models predicted cardiovascular events better than guideline-recommended tools - a step toward prevention that catches more at-risk people earlier.
europmc-pmc6621996: Systematic reviews take months of expert slog - much of it automatable. This practical guide tours machine-learning tools that speed each step: finding studies, screening them, and pulling out data. The authors show where automation already works, where humans must stay in charge, and how to combine the two.
europmc-pmc6702196: A blood draw might forecast how long you live. Scanning the metabolic profiles of 44,168 people, researchers found chemical signatures tied to the risk of dying from any cause. The observational study suggests a standardized metabolomics readout could one day flag high-risk individuals long before symptoms appear.
europmc-pmc6770596: Salt and blood pressure are old adversaries - and the evidence still favors less salt. This review confirms the sodium-hypertension link: cutting salt lowers pressure and trims hypertension risk. The familiar advice stands on solid ground.
europmc-pmc6770896: Triple-negative breast cancer is the toughest subtype - no hormone targets, relentless growth. Chemotherapy is the main weapon, but resistance comes fast. This review maps how TNBC dodges chemo and how researchers plan to fight back. The challenge is steep; the strategies are getting smarter.
gao-gaoreports-b-309996: A 2007 GAO ruling on two linked contract fights from Earl Industries, LLC, a ship repair firm. The company said the Navy's award missed the mark; the ruling weighs each protest point in turn. For yards bidding on Navy fix-up work, the call shows how GAO judges a tight race — and how repeat filings from one firm get handled.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1196: How many troops sought out as conscientious objectors during an unpopular war? GAO counted in 2007 — and the number was tiny next to the size of the armed forces. The report swaps heat for math on a charged question, tallying formal objector bids to show what the moral-exit lane really looked like.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-996: Four artificial jaw joints won FDA approval — but did the science hold up? GAO's 2007 report puts the agency's green light for TMJ implants under the microscope. The findings probe whether the proof of safety matched the promise, for patients whose jaw pain left them few other options.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1096: The one-stop job shops were still finding their feet in 2007 — GAO's report says the workforce system's storefronts kept evolving, but Labor needed to step up. The findings track a well-meant idea — one door for every job hunter — bumping against the realities of funding and follow-through.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-696: The war commands were fuzzy on flu duty in 2007 — GAO's report says the Pentagon's regional commands needed sharper outbreak roles. The findings map the preparedness gaps. The report's warning: a pandemic would not wait for the chain of command to sort itself out.
gao-gaoreports-b-299496: Raymond Associates doubled its May 2007 protest — two case numbers, one contract fight — and GAO's combined ruling settles both claims at once. The firm challenged the awards as unfair; the call weighs each claim carefully. Paired protests get a single, thorough answer from the referee.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-296: The New Markets tax credit was drawing investors in 2007, and GAO's report says it appeared to boost investment in poor communities, with caveats. The findings balance hope and doubt. The report asks whether the tax break bought real renewal. The jury was still out.
openalex-w7204250996: Some people form blood clots again and again, and the cause often goes unnamed. This article studies antiphospholipid syndrome, an underdiagnosed culprit behind repeat thrombosis: how it works, how it shows up, and how to treat it. The authors make the case for suspecting it sooner. A clinical review that could change how doctors chase recurring clots.
openalex-w7204469096: Brazil's private health plans follow national rules, but care looks very different from state to state. This article argues that one-size regulation fails unequal territories, and makes the case for adapting oversight to local realities. The authors study the mismatch between uniform rules and diverse ground. A health-policy paper on governing a continent-sized system.
pmc-13462796: This 2026 clinical study aims to predict when ovarian function will decline in girls and women with Turner syndrome, a chromosomal condition affecting development. Early warning would help patients and families plan for fertility and hormone care. The paper builds toward practical tools for a group that needs clearer timelines.
pmc-13458396: A 2026 molecular genetics paper showing that human PMS1 — working outside the classic mismatch-repair pathway — teams up with the MBD4 enzyme to fix a common DNA lesion: methylated CpG sites damaged by deamination. The study maps a backup repair route the cell uses to protect its genetic code. Finding new repair partnerships matters for understanding mutation and cancer.
pmc-13434196: This 2026 pediatrics paper linked social drivers of health — housing, income, neighborhood conditions — to hospitalizations for childhood asthma. Asthma flares aren't just medical; they're social. The findings argue that preventing hospitalizations means addressing the conditions children live in.
pmc-13428796: This 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis compared robotic versus laparoscopic inguinal hernia repair. Robotic surgery promises precision; the pooled evidence tests whether patients actually do better. The comparison helps hospitals and surgeons weigh the considerable cost of the robot.
pmc-13334196: A 2026 Finnish nationwide register study tracking time trends in excess mortality among people with bipolar disorder from 2000 to 2023. The mortality gap is psychiatry's starkest inequality. The trends show whether it is narrowing.
pmc-13508696: In this 2026 paper, metabolic crisis and TRPM4 activation were shown to cause QT prolongation — a dangerous heart rhythm change — in TANGO2 deficiency disorder. The mechanism links a rare metabolic disease to cardiac risk. The finding has direct implications for patient monitoring.
pmc-13469896: A 2026 review of progress on novel compounds for bone metabolism disorders, focusing on osteoporosis and beyond. New bone drugs are urgently needed. The review surveys the pipeline.
pmc-13426296: This 2026 secondary sensitivity analysis reallocated receptor contributions after removing literature-derived weights in an integrated Ki-DDD-TWAS pipeline. The methods paper stress-tests its own assumptions. The sensitivity analysis is the rigor.
pmc-13538796: A 2026 Spanish multicenter retrospective observational study of real-world effectiveness and safety of finerenone in type 2 diabetes with chronic kidney disease. The kidney-protective drug's real-world performance was measured. The study confirms trial findings.
pmc-13525496: This 2026 nursing study examined nursing risk management's impact on quality of life, complications, and satisfaction in PCI patients. The management approach improved outcomes. The study quantifies the benefit.
pmc-13531196: In this 2026 cardiac surgery paper, resources defined operability after pulmonary endarterectomy. The resource constraint shaped surgical decisions. The paper examines the reality.
pmc-13517996: This 2026 case report described clinical application of intravenous lipid emulsion therapy in cocaine-associated cardiac arrest. The lipid rescue worked. The case supports the protocol.
pmc-13483096: This 2026 review examined gamma-delta T cells in ischemic stroke from the brain-gut axis perspective. The unconventional T cells' stroke role was synthesized. The axis lens is the framing.
pmc-13457496: In this 2026 paper, dimensionality reduction served offline Arabic sign language alphabet recognition using deep learning. The signs were recognized efficiently. The reduction is the optimization.
pmc-13471996: A 2026 SERENA-6 paper on visual patient-reported outcomes and safety of camizestrant for emerging ESR1-mutant advanced breast cancer during first-line endocrine therapy. The trial's patient perspective was reported. The outcomes are the data.
pmc-13369296: A 2026 paper with physiological and behavioral characterization of a novel steroid sulfatase-deficient mouse. The knockout mouse was profiled. The characterization serves neurodevelopment research.
pmc-13472896: A 2026 psychiatry paper: "Nightmares matter" — rethinking suicide risk assessment and intervention in depression. The bad dreams' predictive power was argued. The rethinking is the clinical call.
pmc-13439696: A 2026 Arabidopsis paper: natural variation modified centromere-proximal meiotic crossover frequency and segregation distortion. The recombination landscape varied. The modification is the genetic insight.
pmc-13452996: A 2026 case report and literature review of a CREST-associated ruptured right middle cerebral artery aneurysm. The autoimmune-aneurysm link was documented. The case is the rarity.
pmc-13424496: In this 2026 paper, preclinical testing was redefined — human-relevant alternatives beyond animal models. The animal-free future was charted. The redefining is the paradigm shift.
pmc-13441196: This 2026 paper introduced PRIMER — Premedical Introduction to Mentored Emergency Research, connecting undergraduate assistants and emergency medicine residents in a community hospital (the title is truncated). The mentorship program was described. The connecting is the educational model.
pmc-13426896: A 2026 thematic qualitative study of OCD patients' perspectives on AI's role in therapy and treatment. The patients' views were centered. The perspectives guide ethical AI.
pmc-13597496: This 2026 paper examined reservation policies and equity in national park access. The booking systems' fairness was studied. The equity question is the policy finding.
pmc-13492196: A 2026 veterinary paper on microbial colonization of the neonatal beef calf gastrointestinal tract — limited influence of birth delivery method across five anatomical regions. The calves' gut microbes were mapped. The limited influence is the finding.
pmc-13554896: A 2026 case report on managing aortic regurgitation and dynamic aortic thrombus in a patient with left ventricular assist device. The LVAD complication was navigated. The managing is the mechanical circulatory support lesson.
arxiv-2606-15996: A theoretical physics paper linking information theory to gravity. It takes a generalized idea of entropy (disorder) proposed by Sharma and Mittal, derives limits on how much information a region can hold, and asks what those limits imply for gravity at cosmic scales. The work is speculative and aimed at physicists studying quantum gravity.
arxiv-2606-16096: Mid-infrared light reveals chemical fingerprints, but capturing full spectral images in one shot is hard. This paper demonstrates snapshot spectral imaging in the mid-infrared using nonlinear radial dispersion — spreading light by color through a nonlinear optical trick. The result is a camera-like system for chemists and materials scientists who need instant spectral pictures.
arxiv-2606-16196: AI models can be confidently wrong on inputs unlike their training data — "out-of-distribution" cases. This paper builds an interpretable detector that spots such cases by perturbing the model's internal representations and watching what breaks. The goal is OOD warnings that humans can understand, not just a single confidence score.
arxiv-2606-16296: Gravitational waves ripple through everything, including quantum fields. This theoretical physics paper studies how a resonant scalar field responds to gravitational waves in real time, focusing on the "ultraviolet structure" — the behavior at the smallest scales. It targets researchers in quantum field theory in curved spacetime.
arxiv-2606-16396: Scarred pics get mended by swap-in scrubbers — yet wild scrubs can stray. SP3 leashes them to a ball-shell of sane picks: each mend must sit on the orb of sound choices. Pic-fix pros get truer mends with proof of stay-in-bounds.
arxiv-2606-16696: Gait spans man, bot, and beast — yet most gait-tapes serve one hide. VENOM is one wide gait-net for all-hide tread trails: a single eye that trails each tread, hide no bar. For toon, bot, and gait crews. One eye, each tread.
arxiv-2606-16796: Cosmic rays ionize the gas where stars are born, shaping chemistry. Using HINSA observations (a radio technique), this paper studies cosmic-ray ionization in two star-forming clouds, IC 348 and NGC 1333 — finding evidence for strong low-energy cosmic rays. It is for astrochemists.
